title: The Sluice Keeper
subtitle: Metal impacts against moving water
text: A county painter came to redraw the old sluice gate, but found that someone had quietly replaced its measuring ruler. At dawn he climbed mossy steps, his wooden clogs tapping the stone, while water ran steadily through the sluice tunnel. He tapped the ruler with a small hammer: the old wood sounded dull, but the new wood answered with a hollow knock. He pulled a hidden nail, and an iron plate clanged into a basin. Outside, the gatekeeper rang the departure bell. The painter held up the faulty ruler; the boatmen stopped rowing, leaving only small waves lapping the bank. The gate was sealed before it could be opened by mistake.
